scientific_principle: NetworkSedimentTransporter is a Lagrangian bed-material model: sediment is carried as parcels through the links of a river network, with per-link transport times derived from the Wilcock-Crowe (1971) relation applied to the local slope, flow depth, width, and active-layer grain statistics. Two scientific invariants must hold on any network, hydraulic state, or sediment record. (1) Finiteness/physical realizability: every stored quantity the workflow inspects — node elevations (after alluvium adjustment), parcel grain size, parcel volume, and parcel position along its link — must remain finite and physically bounded (position within [0, link length]); a division by a zero width, depth, link length, active-layer thickness, or slope produces NaN/Inf and is the 'finite scientific inconsistency' the reproduction flags. (2) Sediment volume balance: with abrasion disabled and no new pulses, the sum of parcel volumes still in the network plus the volume that has left through the outlet (boundary flux) must equal the initial pulse volume; abrasion, when enabled, may only reduce volume by the computed abrasion loss. Transport must also respect the slope threshold (no motion below it) and must be independent of arbitrary node/link labelling of the same physical network.
violated_invariant: The time-stepping calculation produces non-finite (NaN/Inf) values in the stored river state and/or breaks the sediment volume balance (in-network volume plus boundary outflow no longer equals the initial volume minus abrasion loss), so the tracked parcel motion is no longer physically consistent.
observable_symptom: The public workflow runs to completion but its observation of the downstream history and stored state is non-finite (and volume/position bookkeeping is inconsistent), so the reproduction is reported as a pre-fix scientific failure rather than a completed workflow.
acceptance_checks: On a fresh single-link network with a sediment pulse and abrasion disabled, parcel grain size, volume, and position and the node elevations all remain finite after many time steps.

With abrasion disabled and no new pulses, the sum of all parcel volumes (those still in the network plus those that have exited through the outlet) equals the initial pulse volume within numerical tolerance.
Each parcel's position along its current link stays within [0, link_length] and is monotonically non-decreasing until the parcel leaves the network, after which it is recorded as off-network.
A parcel on a link whose slope is below the transport threshold does not advance, while a parcel on a sufficiently steep link with the same hydraulic conditions advances downstream.
On a branching network with pulses entering at multiple headwater links, the finiteness and volume-balance invariants still hold as parcels merge and travel to the outlet.
Relabelling the nodes and links of an otherwise identical network leaves the parcels' final volumes and positions unchanged (representation invariance).

import numpy as np
from landlab import NetworkModelGrid
from landlab.components import FlowDirectorSteepest, NetworkSedimentTransporter
from landlab.data_record import DataRecord
def mk(coords,links,elev,elems,vol=1.0):
    n=len(elems); g=NetworkModelGrid(len(links),node_coordinates=coords,link_nodes=links)
    g.add_field("topographic_elevation","node"); g.set_val("topographic_elevation",elev)
    for f,v in [("flow_width",5.0),("flow_depth",1.0),("discharge",5.0),("drainage_area",1000.0)]:
        g.add_field(f,"link"); g.set_val(f,np.full(len(links),v))
    fd=FlowDirectorSteepest(g); fd.run_one_step()
    vs={k:np.full((n,1),float(v)) for k,v in [("D",.05),("density",2650.),("volume",vol),("location_at_link",0.),("active_layer",1),("abrasion_rate",0.)]}
    vs["element_id"]=np.array(elems,dtype=int).reshape(n,1)
    p=DataRecord(variables=vs,items={},times=[0.0])
    return g,p,NetworkSedimentTransporter(g,p,fd)
try:
    g,p,t=mk([[0,0],[100,0]],[[0,1]],[10.,0.],[0])
    L=float(g.link_length[0]); ok=True; prev=0.0; exited=False
    for _ in range(300):
        t.run_one_step(1.0)
        loc=float(p.dataset.location_at_link.values[0,-1]); eid=int(p.dataset.element_id.values[0,-1])
        if eid<0: exited=True; break
        if loc<-1e-9 or loc>L+1e-9 or loc<prev-1e-9: ok=False; break
        prev=loc
    ok=ok and exited
    print("PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
except Exception as e:
    print("FAIL",type(e).__name__,e)

import numpy as np
from landlab import NetworkModelGrid
from landlab.components import FlowDirectorSteepest, NetworkSedimentTransporter
from landlab.data_record import DataRecord
def run(coords,links,elev,elems):
    n=len(elems); g=NetworkModelGrid(len(links),node_coordinates=coords,link_nodes=links)
    g.add_field("topographic_elevation","node"); g.set_val("topographic_elevation",elev)
    for f,v in [("flow_width",5.0),("flow_depth",1.0),("discharge",5.0),("drainage_area",1000.0)]:
        g.add_field(f,"link"); g.set_val(f,np.full(len(links),v))
    fd=FlowDirectorSteepest(g); fd.run_one_step()
    vs={k:np.full((n,1),float(v)) for k,v in [("D",.05),("density",2650.),("volume",1.0),("location_at_link",0.),("active_layer",1),("abrasion_rate",0.)]}
    vs["element_id"]=np.array(elems,dtype=int).reshape(n,1)
    p=DataRecord(variables=vs,items={},times=[0.0]); t=NetworkSedimentTransporter(g,p,fd)
    for _ in range(60): t.run_one_step(1.0)
    return p
try:
    cA=[[0,1],[0,-1],[50,0],[100,0]]; lA=[[0,2],[1,2],[2,3]]; eA=[20.,20.,10.,0.]
    pA=run(cA,lA,eA,[0,1])
    perm=[3,2,1,0]; inv=[0]*4
    for o,nw in enumerate(perm): inv[nw]=o
    cB=[cA[inv[j]] for j in range(4)]; lB=[[perm[a],perm[b]] for a,b in lA]; eB=[eA[inv[j]] for j in range(4)]
    pB=run(cB,lB,eB,[0,1])
    ok=np.allclose(pA.dataset.volume.values[:,-1],pB.dataset.volume.values[:,-1],atol=1e-6) and np.allclose(pA.dataset.location_at_link.values[:,-1],pB.dataset.location_at_link.values[:,-1],atol=1e-6)
    print("PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
except Exception as e:
    print("FAIL",type(e).__name__,e)

anti_hardcoding: Clamping velocities, slopes, or alluvium depths to finite constants (or to zero) to silence NaN/Inf, which would break the slope-threshold motion probe and the distance/position invariants.
Zeroing or deleting parcels that reach the outlet so the in-network volume sum looks conserved, which breaks the boundary-outflow accounting and the on-network/off-network bookkeeping.

Special-casing the public case by network size, link count, or node count (e.g., only guarding link 0) so the smoke case passes while branching, relabeled, or differently sized networks still produce non-finite state.
Hardcoding node elevations or parcel volumes to fixed finite values after stepping instead of repairing the division/slope/depth calculation that generated the non-finite values.
Returning a fixed 'finite' observation or precomputed downstream history rather than actually running the time-stepping calculation.
evidence_notes: instruction.md and reproduce.py both center on a 'finite' observation: reproduce.py records result.finite and only reports workflow_completed when finite (plus pulse/state/on-network/boundary/distance checks) hold, so the injected defect most plausibly emits NaN/Inf in the stored state or downstream history.

The transporter outline places the arithmetic at risk in _calc_transport_wilcock_crowe (L656, per-link hydraulic/active-layer stats feeding virtual velocity), _adjust_node_elevation (L603) with _calculate_alluvium_depth (L1032, divides by width*length terms), _update_channel_slopes (L450) with _recalculate_channel_slope (L990, divides by dx), and _move_parcel_downstream (L788); run_one_step (L946) orders these. A zero denominator in any of these yields the observed non-finite state.

The _calc_transport_wilcock_crowe snippet is truncated at 'd_act_i =' so the exact defective line is NOT visible in the inventory; I therefore rank several loci and lower confidence rather than assert a single line.

Expected to FAIL before the repair: finite_state_single_link, volume_balance_with_outflow, position_bounded_monotonic_exit, branching_balance_finite, and slope_threshold_no_motion (all read state that a non-finite/incorrect transport step corrupts). label_permutation_invariance is a representation-equivalence check that may already pass pre-fix if the defect is not label-dependent; it guards against shallow fixes that special-case the fixture labelling.

Probes pass the required flow_director (FlowDirectorSteepest) to NetworkSedimentTransporter and build parcels via the DataRecord variables/items/times constructor with element_id as a time-varying variable, matching the '[:, self._time_idx]' access pattern seen in the _calc_transport_wilcock_crowe snippet.

API assumptions that could make a probe error (caught and printed as FAIL) if wrong: grid fields flow_width/flow_depth/discharge/drainage_area at link, topographic_elevation at node, and off-network parcels marked by element_id < 0; the volume balance is stated as in-network plus boundary outflow with abrasion disabled, per the critic's correction.

workflow/river_experiment.py (run_experiment, _distance_from_outlet, _make_parcels) is the working reference setup; probes mirror its public-API usage but build fresh networks rather than loading the fixture.
